title: [Complete IELTS 5.0 - 6.5] - Out of Africa: Solar energy from Sahara

parts.passageHtml:
{[Vivienne Walt reports on how the Sahara Desert could offer a truly green solution to Europe’s energy problems.][339039]}

{[A.][339058]} {[For years, the Sahara has been regarded by many Europeans as a terra incognita* of little economic value or importance.][339059]} {[But this idea may soon change completely.][339078]} {[Politicians and scientists on both sides of the Mediterranean are beginning to focus on the Sahara’s potential to provide power for Europe in the future.][339086]} {[They believe the desert’s true value comes from the fact that it is dry and empty.][339112]} {[Some areas of the Sahara reach 45 degrees centigrade on many afternoons.][339129]} {[It is, in other words, a gigantic natural storehouse of solar energy.][339142]}

{[B.][339155]} {[A few years ago, scientists began to calculate just how much energy the Sahara holds.][339157]} {[They were astonished at the answer.][339172]} {[In theory, a 90,600 square kilometer chunk of the Sahara- smaller than Portugal and a little over 1% of its total area- could yield the same amount of electricity as all the world’s power plants combined.][339179]} {[A smaller square of 15,500 square kilometers about the size of Connecticut could provide electricity for Europe’s 500 million people.][339213]} {[‘I admit I was skeptical until I did the calculations myself,’ says Michael Pawlyn, director of Exploration Architecture, one of three British environmental companies comprising the Sahara Forest Project, which is testing solar plants in Oman and the United Arab Emirates.][339233]} {[Pawlyn calls the Sahara’s potential ‘staggering’.][339271]}

{[C. At the moment, no one is proposing the creation of a solar power station the size of a small country.][339279]} {[But a relatively well-developed technology exists, which proponents say could turn the Sahara’s heat and sunlight into a major source of electricity- Concentrating Solar Power (CSP).][339298]} {[Unlike solar panels, which convert sunlight directly into electricity, CSP utilizes mirrors which focus light on water pipes or boilers to produce very hot steam to operate the turbines of generators.][339326]} {[Small CSP plants have produced power in California’s Mojave Desert since the 1980s.][339357]} {[The Sahara Forest Project proposes building CSP plants in areas below sea level (the Sahara has several such depressions) so that sea water can flow into them.][339371]} {[This water would then be purified and used for powering turbines and washing dust off the mirrors.][339401]} {[Waste water would then supply irrigation to areas around the stations, creating lush oases – hence the ‘forest’ in the group’s name.][339419]}

{[D. But producing significant quantities of electricity means building huge arrays of mirrors and pipes across hundreds of miles of remote desert, which is expensive.][339442]} {[Gerry Wolff, an engineer who heads DESERTEC, an international consortium of solar-power scientists, says they have estimated it will cost about $59 billion to begin transmitting power from the Sahara by 2020][339467]}

{[E. Building plants is just part of the challenge.][339499]} {[One of the drawbacks to CSP technology is that it works at maximum efficiency only in sunny, hot climates - and deserts tend to be distant from population centres.][339508]} {[To supply Europe with 20% of its electricity needs, more than 19,300 kilometres of cables would need to be laid under the Mediterranean, says Gunnar Asplund, head of HVDC research at ABB Power Technologies in Ludvika, Sweden.][339537]} {[Indeed, to use renewable sources of power, including solar, wind and tidal, Europe will need to build completely new electrical grids.][339574]} {[That’s because existing infrastructures, built largely for the coal-fired plants that supply 80% of Europe’s power, would not be suitable for carrying the amount of electricity generated by the Sahara.][339596]} {[Germany’s government-run Aerospace Centre, which researches energy, estimates that replacing those lines could raise the cost of building solar plants in the Sahara and sending significant amounts of power to Europe to about $485 billion over the next 40 years.][339627]} {[Generous government subsidies will be needed.][339669]} {[‘Of course it costs a lot of money,’ says Asplund.][339676]} {[‘It’s a lot cheaper to burn coal than to make solar power in the Sahara.][339686]} {[’][339702]}

{[F. Meanwhile, some companies are getting started.][339705]} {[Seville engineering company Abengoa is building one solar-thermal plant in Algeria and another in Morocco, while a third is being built in Egypt by a Spanish-Japanese joint venture.][339712]} {[The next step will be to get cables in place.][339739]} {[Although the European Parliament has passed a law that aids investors who help the continent reach its goal of getting 20% of its power from renewable energy by 2020, it could take years to create the necessary infrastructure.][339750]}

{[G. Nicholas Dunlop, secretary-general of the London-based NGO e-Parliament, thinks companies should begin transmitting small amounts of solar power as soon as the North African plants begin operating, by linking a few cable lines under the Med.][339790]} {['I call it the Lego method,’ he says.][339827]} {[‘Build it piece by piece.][339836]} {[’ If It can be shown that power from the Sahara can be produced profitably, he says, companies and governments will soon jump in.][339842]} {[ If they do, perhaps airplane passengers flying across the Sahara will one day count the mirrors and patches of green instead of staring at sand.][339866]}

{[*terra incognita - Latin, meaning ‘an unknown land'][339893]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 5:

Which paragraph contains the following information?

NB You may use any letter more than once.

questions.text: A mention of systems which could not be used
questions.explanationHtml:
Building plants is just part of the challenge. One of the drawbacks to CSP technology is that it works at maximum efficiency only in sunny, hot climates - and deserts tend to be distant from population centres. To supply Europe with 20% of its electricity needs, more than 19,300 kilometres of cables would need to be laid under the Mediterranean

(Indeed, to use renewable sources of power, including solar, wind and tidal, Europe will need to build completely new electrical grids)

 

=> E

đây là điều không tưởng “could not be used”bởi vì cả “Europe” phải lắp lại “electrical grids”nếu muốn dùng “solar power”

questions.text: Estimates of the quantity of power the Sahara could produce
questions.explanationHtml:
(scientists began to calculate just how much energy the Sahara holds)

(In theory, a 90,600 square kilometer chunk of the Sahara- smaller than Portugal and a little over 1% of its total area- could yield the same amount of electricity as all the world’s power plants combined. A smaller square of 15,500 square kilometers about the size of Connecticut could provide electricity for Europe’s 500 million people)

 

=> B

paraphrase “yield” thành “produce” và “holds”, “how much energy” thành “the quantity of power”

questions.text: A suggestion for how to convince organisations about the Sahara's potential
questions.explanationHtml:
thinks companies should begin transmitting small amounts of solar power as soon as the North African plants begin operating, by linking a few cable lines under the Med. 'I call it the Lego method,’ he says. ‘Build it piece by piece.’ If It can be shown that power from the Sahara can be produced profitably, he says, companies and governments will soon jump in

 

=> G

“produce profitably” chính là “potential” của Sahara, nếu không xây dựng được 1 lượt, thì xây dựng “piece by piece” từng bước nhỏ => các “oragnisations” = “companies and goverments” sẽ bị “convinced” thuyết phục và “jump in” tham gia

questions.text: A short description of the Sahara at present
questions.explanationHtml:
For years, the Sahara has been regarded by many Europeans as a terra incognita of little economic value or importance

But this idea may soon change completely.

It is, in other words, a gigantic natural storehouse of solar energy.

 

=> A

“regarded” nghĩa là “đuợc xem như là”  một cách để cho “description” miêu tả

“Years ago” => Sahara = “terra incognita”

Now => Sahara = “a gigantic natural store house of solar energy”

questions.text: A comparison of the costs of two different energy sources
questions.explanationHtml:
‘Of course it costs a lot of money,’ says Asplund. ‘It’s a lot cheaper to burn coal than to make solar power in the Sahara.’ 

 

=> E

“cheaper” thể hiện sự so sánh “comparison" giữa “burn coal” và “solar power in Sahara”

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 6 - 9:

Match each statement with the correct organisation using A-G.

List of Organisations

A. Exploration Architecture

E. Abengoa

B. DESERTEC

F. The European Parliament

C. ABB Power Technologies

G. e-Parliament

D. Aerospace Centre

questions.text: They have set a time for achieving an objective.
questions.explanationHtml:
đoạn 6 (Although the European Parliament has passed a law that aids investors who help the continent reach its goal of getting 20% of its power from renewable energy by 2020, it could take years to create the necessary infrastructure.)

F (scan ý “set a time” => tìm các mốc thời gian => chi có “European Parliament” muốn “reach its goal” đạt đuợc mục tiêu “by 2020”

questions.text: They believe that successful small-scale projects will demonstrate that larger projects are possible.
questions.explanationHtml:
đoạn 7 (Nicholas Dunlop, secretary-general of the London-based NGO e-Parliament, thinks companies should begin transmitting small amounts of solar power as soon as the North African plants begin operating, by linking a few cable lines under the Med. 'I call it the Lego method,’ he says. ‘Build it piece by piece’)

(If they do, perhaps airplane passengers flying across the Sahara will one day count the mirrors and patches of green instead of staring at stand)

 

G (“small-scale projects” ở đây là “small amounts of solar power”, “larger projects” là toàn bộ sahara được phủ bởi “mirrors and patches”

questions.text: They have a number of renewable energy projects under construction.
questions.explanationHtml:
đoạn 6 (Seville engineering company Abengoa is building one solar-thermal plant in Algeria and another in Morocco, while a third is being built in Egypt by a Spanish-Japanese joint venture)

E (paraphrase “being built” thành “under consruction” trong đáp án, có 3 “renewable projects” là “solar-thermal plant” nhà máy nhiệt điện mặt trời ở Algeria, Morocco, và Egypt)

questions.text: They are already experimenting with solar- energy installations in other parts of the world.
questions.explanationHtml:
đoạn 2 (director of Exploration Architecture, one of three British environmental companies comprising the Sahara Forest Project, which is testing solar plants in Oman and the United Arab Emirates)

A ( paraphrase “testing” thành “experimental” trong đáp án, “solar-energy installations” = “solar plants”, “other parts of the world” ở đây là “Oman” và “ the United Arab Emirates”)

questionSets.contentHtml:
Concentrating Solar Power (CSP)

Unlike solar panels, CSP concentrates the sun's rays on boilers by using 10 The resulting heat produces high-temperature 11 , which in turn moves the turbines which generate electricity. CSP plants will be situated in 12  to allow sea water to run in. This, when purified, can be used to wash the equipment.  The resulting dirty water will be used for 13  around the power plant, and in this way oases will be formed.
